clue.text: Getting quieter, making faint insinuation in speech

indicators.note: in speech tells the solver the phrase is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: faint means dim and an insinuation is an innuendo, so the phrase is dim innuendo

explanation.surface: Someone lowers their voice while dropping a sly hint into what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'dim innuendo' runs together into the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminuendo is a passage in music where the volume gradually drops, a direction to play more softly.

clue.text: In disaster state of mind is upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mood is a state of mind

explanation.surface: During a catastrophe someone's frame of mind is badly shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom means ruin or a terrible fate, close to disaster.

clue.text: Perhaps the wife will make the tea

definitions.meaning: a spouse or partner can be called one's ...; perhaps signals an example
a South American herbal infusion brewed from yerba leaves, drunk from a gourd

explanation.surface: A husband hopes his wife will put the kettle on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a spouse or partner and also the South American infusion made from holly leaves.

clue.text: Once more going up with flyers, everyone initially sees New York city

indicators.note: going up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: again means once more
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is a body of flyers
all means everyone

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Pilots climbing once more see a city in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is a city in New York State beside the famous waterfalls.

clue.text: Scarlet leaf halfway up tree

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the whole run from bottom to top

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: halfway keeps the first half of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A red leaf hangs partway up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the run from the bottom, so the red-plus-half-leaf combination is turned round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree or shrub with white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Man given partner was hopeless

parts.note: Des is a man's name, short for Desmond
paired means matched with a partner

explanation.surface: A man finally got a partner after feeling hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: To have despaired is to have lost all hope, so it matches was hopeless as a past verb.

clue.text: A famous Spanish soldier becoming vitriolic

parts.note: El Cid was the celebrated medieval Castilian warrior Rodrigo Díaz

explanation.surface: A legendary Spanish warrior turns bitter and sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid remarks are caustic and biting, just as vitriolic ones are; vitriol is itself an old name for sulphuric acid.

clue.text: Dog, following docking

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
tailing means following closely

explanation.surface: A dog trots after a boat as it comes into dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' looks nautical but means cutting short, as with a dog's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking means cutting short, as a tail is docked, so it matches curtailing.

clue.text: Destroyed damaged model I dropped

indicators.note: damaged suggests things knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
shed means dropped or cast off

explanation.surface: A broken model slipped from someone's hands and was wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolished means knocked down or wrecked, a synonym of destroyed.

clue.text: Bizarre and unpopular line put to an attractive girl

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion or favour
taken as written
a dish is slang for a good-looking person

explanation.surface: A strange, unwelcome chat-up line is tried on a pretty girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strikingly odd or unfamiliar, a close synonym of bizarre.

clue.text: Nanny may use this soft butter

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
read as one that butts: a ram butts with its head

explanation.surface: A children's nurse spreads something mild on her bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but a thing that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny pushes a baby around in a pram, so the clue defines it by a typical user.

clue.text: Eat with unfamiliar chaps for a lack of good relationship

annotationWithheld.why: 'Eat with unfamiliar chaps for a lack of good relationship' (12), as printed: E + STRANGE MEN + T gives the answer but Eat supplies an A that no word removes
annotationWithheld.clue: Eat with unfamiliar chaps for a lack of good relationship

clue.text: Fortification in Danish war all going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong suggests things falling into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In a war with the Danes, everything starts to go badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges DANISH WAR as HADRIANSW; ALL stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor Hadrian built a defensive stone barrier across northern England, a fortification.

clue.text: Something that enabled Mr Chips to make his mark?

definitions.text: Something that enabled Mr Chips to make his mark?

parts.words: Something that enabled Mr Chips to make his mark?
parts.note: Mr Chips is the schoolmaster of Goodbye, Mr Chips; making a mark here is literally writing with chalk in front of a class

explanation.surface: What helped a famous schoolteacher make his name?
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers write in chalk on a dark board fixed to the classroom wall.

clue.text: Shattered, as carpenter's fingers may be?

definitions.meaning: a woodworker's fingers can end up with slivers of wood stuck in them

explanation.definitionFit: The word means broken into shards and also pierced by slivers of wood.

clue.text: Circuit made by plane coming in, one in the far north

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
an aircraft arriving to touch down is literally a lander

explanation.surface: A plane completes a loop of the airfield before landing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laplander is a native of Lapland, the region in the Arctic north of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Remove smell from little old woman who's been in the river

indicators.note: who's been in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England–Wales border
O is a short form of old
Doris is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who went in the river needs freshening up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deodorise is to take away or mask an unpleasant odour.

clue.text: Official lists of breakfast food

definitions.meaning: ... are official registers of names, as in electoral ...
bread ... are commonly eaten at breakfast

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both formal registers of names and small loaves of bread eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Country church in middle of glade

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: middle of picks out the central letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A rural chapel stands in the middle of a woodland clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the church but is the definition; 'middle of' takes the central A of glade.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a nation in East Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Regulation military supplies one imported

indicators.note: imported means brought inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ordnance is military stores, especially weapons and ammunition
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Army equipment includes a single item brought in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative rule or decree, so it is a synonym of regulation.

clue.text: Courage shown by batsman: one could get cap knocked off!

definitions.text: one could get cap knocked off

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
an opener is a batsman who opens the innings in cricket

explanation.surface: A brave cricketer faces a ball that could knock his cap off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the two opening batsmen face the first balls; the cap is a bottle top, not headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle opener is a tool that prises the metal cap off a bottle.

clue.text: Educated, but lacking a CD to review piece of music

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking back, so the letters run backwards
lacking means going without, so letters are removed

parts.note: the letters A, C and D, removed from the word as they occur

explanation.surface: A learned person without a disc cannot listen back to a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes C, A and D from EDUCATED, leaving EDUTE; 'to review' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a short composition written to practise a technique, so a piece of music.

clue.text: Stuff said to be in the post

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to jam is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Some stuffing is supposedly sent through the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like mail but is a doorpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Way McBeal. finally leaves is an irritation to the viewer

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: style means manner or way

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Ally McBeal's departure from the screen irritates television viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes L from McBeal; it 'leaves' STYLE. Ally McBeal was a US TV legal comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, irritating the eye that views.

clue.text: Cautious with a wife-swapping, being on the wrong course

indicators.note: a wife-swapping says the letters A and W change places within the word

parts.note: wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A careful person who swaps partners finds life going off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a wife-swapping' means A and W (wife) trade places in WARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means off course or askew, so something going awry has strayed from the right path.

clue.text: Officer taking place overseas, one renting accommodation

parts.note: lieu is French for place, hence overseas
a tenant is someone who rents a home

explanation.surface: An officer posted abroad rents somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the armed forces, so an officer.

clue.text: Dandy is ineffectual person with little energy

parts.note: a dud is a useless person or thing
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A fop is a feeble sort with hardly any get-up-and-go.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is old American slang for a man overly concerned with his clothes, a dandy.

clue.text: Charming Democrat plausible as candidate

parts.note: a candidate who could plausibly win is electable

explanation.surface: A likeable Democrat looks a credible runner for office.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delightful or highly pleasing, close to charming.
